clue.text: Discard a volume of cuttings

parts.note: to discard something is to scrap it, throw it away
a volume is a book, one of a set or simply a bound tome

explanation.surface: Someone throws out an album of newspaper clippings.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: SCRAP (discard) plus BOOK (volume) builds it, and the full sentence also describes the album of clippings itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An album into which newspaper clippings and mementos are pasted is a book of cuttings.

clue.text: Encourage singularly good health

indicators.note: the plural-looking toast is made singular by dropping its final letter

parts.note: the toast 'Cheers!' is said when drinking someone's good health

explanation.surface: A wish for someone's robust wellbeing, offered one at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singularly' removes the S from CHEERS, the drinking toast, as if making a plural noun singular.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone on is to encourage them with shouts of support.

clue.text: Gunnery return with obstinate enthusiasm

indicators.note: the regiment's abbreviation comes back the other way round

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, is the British army's gunnery regiment
dour can mean stern and stubbornly unyielding

explanation.surface: A soldier coming back from artillery duty with grim but stubborn zeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns RA (Royal Artillery) round to AR, followed by DOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardour is passionate eagerness or zeal.

clue.text: Bighead's sheepish or bullish!

parts.note: the head of the word big is its first letter, and the 's links it to what follows
ovine means of or like sheep

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a conceited person is either timid or aggressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bighead' is not a conceited person: read it as 'big head', the first letter of big, B. Add OVINE (sheep-like) to get a word meaning ox-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Bovine describes cattle, so a bull-like creature is bovine.

clue.text: It is fantastic to be out and about

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word for about or concerning

explanation.surface: Being out and about on the town is wonderful fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is taken as written; 'about' gives RE, as in a letter's 'Re:' line.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré means bizarre or unconventional, far beyond the usual, so wildly fantastic.

clue.text: Old fogey unreliable in navigating the estuary?

definitions.meaning: a person stubbornly resistant to change and new ideas
a boat that keeps lodging in the silt of a tidal river mouth

explanation.definitionFit: A conservative old person is stuck in old ways, and a vessel grounding on a mudbank literally sticks there.

clue.text: Was taken aback and came home first

definitions.text: Was taken aback and came home first

parts.words: Was taken aback and came home first
parts.note: read literally: a jockey was carried on a horse's back, and that mount finished ahead of the field

explanation.surface: Someone was startled, then hurried home ahead of everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' looks like surprise, but means carried on the back of a horse, which then came home first in the race.
explanation.definitionFit: A jockey whose mount won the race was carried to victory on that horse.

clue.text: Absolute commitment to speak of love

definitions.meaning: to voice one's adoration, utter meaning say

explanation.definitionFit: Utter as an adjective means complete and as a verb means say aloud; devotion is both dedication and love.

clue.text: The right to vote belongs to him in the country

indicators.note: the possessive word sits within the country's name

parts.note: France is a European country
something that belongs to him is his

explanation.surface: Only a man living in a certain nation may cast a ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places HIS inside FRANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Franchise is the legal entitlement to cast a ballot in elections.

clue.text: Shall rest awkwardly on an exploding projectile

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are arranged clumsily, so they are to be reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone shall clumsily lay down an explosive shell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkwardly' rearranges SHALLREST.
explanation.definitionFit: A star shell is a shell that bursts in the air to light up a battlefield.

clue.text: Some more curves to be repeated

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A road with extra bends that keep coming again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes a run from 'moRE CURves'.
explanation.definitionFit: To recur is to happen again, which is what being repeated means.

clue.text: Choose to act democratically

explanation.definitionFit: To elect is to select, and in politics specifically to pick representatives by ballot.

clue.text: Heavenly butter

parts.note: a 'butter' is something that butts with its head, and this one is a constellation in the sky

explanation.surface: Praise for a divinely delicious dairy spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not the spread but one who butts, a ram; the heavenly ram is the zodiac sign.
explanation.definitionFit: The constellation and zodiac sign is the Ram, an animal that butts.

clue.text: Fuss with navy on deck

parts.note: ado is fuss or bother
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Sailors making a commotion on board ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' looks nautical beside navy, but it is the verb meaning decorate. ADO + RN (Royal Navy).
explanation.definitionFit: To deck something, as in decking the halls, is to decorate or embellish it.

clue.text: I dislodged coin of a Greek style

indicators.note: the letters of the fodder are knocked out of place and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone knocked loose an ancient Greek coin.
explanation.walkthrough: I stays as written; 'dislodged' rearranges COIN to follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionic is one of the classical architectural orders, with scroll-shaped capitals.

clue.text: Plant on the southern perimeter

parts.note: the perimeter of something is its edge

explanation.surface: A factory located along the southern boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' suggests a factory, but it is a grassy marsh plant. S + EDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedge is a grass-like plant growing in wet ground.

clue.text: Secured from Daniel

indicators.note: the answer is made out of the letters of the name, rearranged

explanation.surface: Something obtained from a man named Daniel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' tells you to make the answer from the letters of DANIEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nailed down is fastened firmly in place.

clue.text: Impressive sort of artist

parts.note: an artist who makes impressions, prints from engraved plates

explanation.surface: Praise for a remarkable painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressive' is not 'remarkable' but 'making impressions', prints from an engraved plate.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist who incises designs on plates with acid and prints from them produces impressions.

clue.text: Had shown displeasure after father left

indicators.note: the abbreviation has departed from the word

parts.note: frowned means showed displeasure with one's face
Fr is the abbreviation for father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: A child scowled once their dad had gone out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' removes FR (Father) from FROWNED.
explanation.definitionFit: Had in the sense of possessed: to have owned something is to have held it as property.

clue.text: Empty talk over the Sahara?

definitions.meaning: the atmosphere above a scorching desert

explanation.definitionFit: Meaningless words are idiomatically puffed-up air, and the air above a desert is literally baking.

clue.text: Warthog strangely without a tumour

indicators.note: the letters of the animal are oddly rearranged
the single letter is dropped from the animal's name before the shuffle

explanation.surface: A wild pig that oddly has no cancerous lump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes A from WARTHOG, and 'strangely' rearranges the remaining WRTHOG.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumour is an abnormal mass of tissue, a swelling or growth.

clue.text: Hot but pleasant outside for the recess

indicators.note: the agreeable word goes round the single letter

parts.note: nice means pleasant or agreeable
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Somewhere warm yet agreeable outdoors to spend a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts NICE around H (hot).
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a shallow alcove set into a wall.

clue.text: Freezing point

parts.note: not the temperature at which water turns solid but a frozen pointed thing

explanation.surface: The temperature at which water turns to ice.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase reads as a temperature, but means a pointed spike that has frozen.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapering spike of frozen dripping water is literally a point that has frozen.

clue.text: Channel Island has the very thing for a recluse

parts.note: Herm is one of the smaller Channel Islands, between Guernsey and Sark
'it' means exactly what is needed, as in 'that's it'

explanation.surface: A small island offers the perfect retreat for someone seeking solitude.
explanation.walkthrough: HERM is a small Channel Island; IT is the very thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit lives alone, withdrawn from society.

clue.text: One way to cook assorted meats

indicators.note: the letters are mixed up like an assortment

explanation.surface: A suggested cooking method for a mixed selection of meats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assorted' rearranges MEATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Steaming is a cooking method using vapour from boiling water.

clue.text: An officer of greater importance

explanation.definitionFit: Major is both an army rank above captain and an adjective meaning more significant.

clue.text: The last notes, lad, from Fingal's Cove'

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'The last notes, lad, from Fingal's Cove'' looks garbled by OCR (Cove for Cave, stray quote); the likely parse FINGAL less G leaves 'notes' plural and 'lad' with no job, and the original text could not be confirmed.
annotationWithheld.clue: The last notes, lad, from Fingal's Cove'

clue.text: There can be no recovery from such an accident

definitions.text: There can be no recovery from such an accident

parts.words: There can be no recovery from such an accident
parts.note: describes a mishap that kills, so nobody gets better afterwards

explanation.surface: A mishap so bad that nothing can be salvaged.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadly accident is one the victim never survives.

clue.text: Topic prone to concern

parts.note: prone to something means subject to it, liable to it
a concern is a matter, an affair

explanation.surface: A theme liable to cause worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prone' is not lying face down but 'liable', as in subject to.
explanation.definitionFit: The topic of a book or talk is what it deals with, its theme.

clue.text: At liberty to choose a form of wrestling

definitions.meaning: free to pick one's own manner of doing something
a wrestling discipline allowing holds on the legs, unlike Greco-Roman

explanation.definitionFit: Freestyle is a wrestling discipline permitting leg holds, and literally means a manner left open.
